question: Is there a task and loss that lets an encoder learn generic, off-the-shelf sentence representations without a particular supervised task in mind?
hypothesis: Abstracting skip-gram to the sentence level (encode a sentence to predict its neighbouring sentences) yields sentence vectors that transfer to many tasks with only a linear model on top.
contributions: Skip-thoughts: unsupervised encoder-decoder objective that reconstructs the previous and next sentence
Vocabulary expansion by linear regression from word2vec space to the encoder embedding space (20,000 to 930,911 words)
Evaluation as a frozen feature extractor with linear models on 8 tasks

method.summary: A GRU encoder maps a sentence to a vector; two conditional-GRU decoders reconstruct the previous and next sentences from it. Trained on BookCorpus, then frozen and used as a feature extractor with linear models (logistic regression, linear ranking embedding) on 8 tasks.
method.task: unsupervised sentence representation learning (sentence-level skip-gram), evaluated by transfer

datasets.name: BookCorpus
datasets.size: 11,038 books; 74,004,228 sentences; 984,846,357 words; 1,316,420 unique words; mean 13 words per sentence
datasets.source: free books by unpublished authors, 16 genres (Zhu et al. 2015)
datasets.preprocessing: training vocabulary of 20,000 words; basic tokenization only at encoding time

datasets.name: MSRP (Microsoft Paraphrase Corpus)
datasets.size: 4076 train pairs (2753 positive), 1725 test pairs (1147 positive)

datasets.name: Microsoft COCO
datasets.size: over 80,000 training images x 5 captions; dev and test 1000 images / 5000 captions each
datasets.split: same splits as Karpathy and Fei-Fei

datasets.name: MR, CR, SUBJ, MPQA, TREC
datasets.split: 10-fold CV for MR, CR, SUBJ, MPQA; predefined split for TREC
datasets.source: Pang and Lee 2005; Hu and Liu 2004; Pang and Lee 2004; Wiebe et al. 2005; Li and Roth 2002

models.name: uni-skip
models.architecture: unidirectional GRU encoder, 2400 dims; two conditional-GRU decoders (previous and next sentence) sharing only vocabulary matrix V
models.context: one sentence in, previous and next sentence out

models.name: bi-skip
models.architecture: bidirectional: forward and backward encoders of 1200 dims each (separate parameters, one reads reversed sentence), concatenated to 2400

models.name: combine-skip
models.architecture: concatenation of uni-skip and bi-skip vectors, 4800 dims, no extra training

models.name: word2vec CBOW vectors
models.architecture: publicly available CBOW embeddings, used for vocabulary expansion

training.objective: sum of log-probabilities of next and previous sentence words conditioned on encoder vector h_i (Eq. 10); vocabulary expansion is un-regularized L2 linear regression W: V_w2v to V_rnn
training.regularisation: gradient clipping when parameter-vector norm exceeds 10

other.init: recurrent matrices orthogonal; non-recurrent weights uniform in [-0.1, 0.1]
other.downstream_ranking: COCO: 1000-d embedding, margin alpha=0.2, k=50 contrastive terms, 15 epochs, keep best dev checkpoint
other.downstream_classifiers: logistic regression with L2 tuned by cross-validation (nested CV for MR, CR, SUBJ, MPQA); SICK uses Tai et al. 2015 setup (logistic regression over 5-point score distribution)

inference.decoding: story generation: condition on a sentence, generate a new one, append and repeat (decoding method not specified)
inference.samples: one 20-sentence sample shown; evaluation single run, seeds not stated

metrics.name: Pearson r, Spearman rho, MSE
metrics.definition: SICK relatedness score (1-5) vs mean of 10 annotators

metrics.name: Recall@K, median rank
metrics.definition: COCO image annotation and image search, 1000-image test

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: MR, CR, SUBJ, MPQA, TREC classification

baselines: SemEval 2014 systems, Tai et al. 2015 LSTM / Tree-LSTM
recursive autoencoders with dynamic pooling (Socher 2011) and top MSRP systems
NB-SVM, MNB, cBoW, GrConv, RNN, BRNN, CNN, AdaSent, Paragraph-vector
eval.protocol: frozen encoder, linear models only, no fine-tuning; no significance tests stated

availability.code: promised ('We will make our encoder publicly available'); NB features use github.com/mesnilgr/nbsvm

evidence.quote: One is a unidirectional encoder with 2400 dimensions, which we subsequently refer to as uni-skip.

results.claim: Vocabulary expansion extends the encoder from a 20,000-word training vocabulary to 930,911 encodable words.
results.setup: linear map from CBOW word2vec space to RNN embedding space, multiword entries removed
results.quote: this results in a vocabulary size of 930,911 words.

results.claim: combine-skip with COCO image-sentence features reaches Pearson r 0.8655 on SICK, on par with the dependency Tree-LSTM (0.8676).
results.setup: SICK test, frozen skip-thought features, logistic regression
results.table: Table 4 left, row combine-skip+COCO, column r

results.claim: combine-skip alone reaches Pearson r 0.8584 on SICK, beating all SemEval 2014 submissions.
results.setup: SICK test, linear model on u.v and |u-v|
results.table: Table 4 left, row combine-skip, column r

results.claim: combine-skip plus basic pairwise features gets 75.8% accuracy / 83.0 F1 on MSRP, competitive with the best (MTMETRICS 77.4 / 84.1).
results.setup: MSRP test, logistic regression, feats from Socher 2011
results.table: Table 4 right, row combine-skip + feats, column Acc

results.claim: combine-skip alone gets 73.0% accuracy on MSRP, above RAE+DP (72.6) without hand-crafted features.
results.table: Table 4 right, row combine-skip, column Acc

results.claim: On COCO image annotation combine-skip gets R@1 33.8 vs m-RNN 41.0; R@10 82.1 vs m-RNN 83.5; median rank 3.
results.setup: COCO 1000-image test, linear embeddings, margin 0.2, k=50
results.table: Table 6, row combine-skip, column R@1 (Image Annotation)

results.claim: On classification, skip-thoughts about match bag-of-words baselines but do not beat task-tuned supervised models; combine-skip MR 76.5, CR 80.1, SUBJ 93.6, MPQA 87.1, TREC 92.2.
results.setup: logistic regression on frozen vectors, 10-fold CV (TREC predefined split)

results.claim: Combining skip-thoughts with bigram NB features gives MR 80.4, a strong new text-classification baseline.
results.table: Table 7, row combine-skip + NB, column MR

results.claim: Each skip-thought model trained for roughly two weeks.
results.note: hardware not stated; quote spans a line

limits: Authors concede supervised task-specific representations beat skip-thoughts on sentiment-type classification.
Only linear evaluators tested; non-linear gains left unexplored.
Model failures on small structural changes (Table 5, e.g. 'tricks' vs 'tricking a person').
No seeds, learning rate, hardware or ablations stated; no significance tests; encoder release only promised.
Authors list unexplored variants: deep encoders/decoders, larger context windows, paragraph encoding, convnet encoders.
Dated: GRU encoder-decoder, 2015 baselines, superseded by transformer pretraining.

terms.definition: vectors induced by encoding a sentence to predict the sentences around it
linear map from word2vec space to encoder embedding space so unseen words can be encoded

lineage.work: Efficient estimation of word representations in vector space (skip-gram, CBOW)
lineage.note: objective abstracts skip-gram to sentence level; CBOW used for vocab expansion

lineage.work: Learning phrase representations using RNN encoder-decoder
Empirical evaluation of gated recurrent neural networks
Distributed representations of sentences and documents (paragraph vector)
